jurisdictions.name: King County (unincorporated areas)
jurisdictions.office: King County Department of Local Services, Permitting Division
notes: Pools accessory to single-family homes and duplexes are exempt from a building permit only if prefabricated, entirely above ground, under 24 inches deep and 5,000 gallons or less, or used temporarily under three months a year.
A pool permit submittal needs a site plan, structural working drawings with engineering calculations or an approved ICC-ES report, and the pool and barrier layout at 1/4 inch = 1 ft.
Energy code information on pool heaters, controls, covers and pumps must be provided with the submittal.
Properties on a septic system need Public Health approval of the pool location before the building permit application.
Single-family residence pools for the family's own use are exempt from Public Health plan review and permits.

jurisdictions.name: Seattle
jurisdictions.office: Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections (SDCI)
notes: Seattle has adopted the 2021 International Residential Code with local amendments, published as the Seattle Residential Code.
The 2021 Seattle Residential Code exempts prefabricated pools with walls entirely above adjacent grade and capacity of 5,000 gallons or less from permits.
SDCI lists accessory swimming pools among standard-plan types and says those plans must be stamped by a Washington state structural engineer with structural notes, soil assumptions and calculations.
The Seattle Residential Code lists Appendix G, Swimming Pools, Spas and Hot Tubs, among its appendices.

jurisdictions.name: Kennewick (Tri-Cities)
jurisdictions.office: City of Kennewick Building Safety Division
notes: Pool permits include an application, a scaled site plan showing pool, fence and heater, and a mechanical permit application if the pool is heated.
The city asks for an ICC-ES report for liner or fiberglass pools, or engineering for a poured-in-place pool.
The city's express checklist for pools is online-only; it also asks for plot plan details such as slopes, easements, setbacks, barrier and equipment locations.
Addresses on septic need an approval letter and stamped plot plan from the Benton Franklin Health Department before applying.
The city's pool requirements sheet cites the 2015 ISPSC for barrier rules, so the edition should be confirmed with the city.

jurisdictions.name: Vancouver
jurisdictions.office: City of Vancouver Community Development Department
notes: Residential building permits (RES) are required for construction, alteration, addition, repair or demolition of residential buildings and structures.
Plans are uploaded through the city's plan submittal site, Avolve ePlans, after the application form is sent to the permit specialists.
The city publishes a Swimming Pool Enclosures and Safety Devices Requirements document among its residential permit forms.
